turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct. Owen found out he had a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"That's the end of it." Is it? The company that sells that checker says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your own school's procedure says the same. So what else do you have, Hale?
I don't need more proof than that.

Procedure 4.3 says software results don't by themselves establish a concern, and I have your school's own copy printed. I'm writing down that you said "I don't need more proof than that." Did you speak to Owen before you entered the zero?
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." My child never lies, and I'm writing that down. Are you calling me a liar too, Hale?
Then I'll be in the principal's office when we're done, with procedure 4.2 and 4.3 in my hand. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in. Answer it, Hale.
